summary: Callback storm triggering soft 429s on Private VPC during large webhook retry wave
description:
Issue summary: Customer reports repeated 429 responses across multiple routes in their Private VPC deployment after a large external retry wave from a third-party webhook consumer. Impact: >10% of webhook callback attempts returned 429 over a 30-minute window for the customer's prod cluster, causing failed downstream ingestion and backpressure in their orchestrator (EdgeForms onboarding flow). Environment: Private deployment (customer-managed VPC), prod-us-west, dedicated path via ingress-proxy -> api-gateway -> orchestrator. Observed: 429s are 'soft' (short-lived, not complete rejection), throttle headers show per-route and tenant quotas being hit, console shows spike in token usage corresponding to 16:10-16:40 UTC. Customer alleges this began after enabling a retry-orchestrator integration on 2026-03-10.

Expected behavior: webhook callback retries should be rate-limited at the edge and queued to avoid rapid tenant token depletion; background flushes should be accounted separately.

Observed behavior: callbacks retried concurrently from the orchestrator created a concentrated burst that exhausted a shared burst pool and surfaced as 429s across multiple routes, including low-priority webhook endpoints.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer reproducer: configure orchestrator to perform up to 8 parallel retry attempts per failed callback.
2) Seed 5k failed webhook deliveries to simulate backlog.
3) Trigger orchestrator retry sweep.
4) Observe 429 spikes in api-gateway and token/burst counters for tenant in console and measured by curl requests against callback endpoints.
5) Verify throttle headers: X-RateLimit-Remaining shows 0 for burst window, Retry-After present on 429s.
logs:
[16:09:58] ingress-proxy: incoming batch of 512 callback replays from 10.4.8.12
[16:10:02] rate-limiter: tenant=edgeforms burst_pool_alloc=512/512 window=60s -> throttle
[16:10:03] api-gateway: response 429 for /callbacks/ingest id=0a3f... Retry-After: 2
[16:10:07] orchestrator: requeueing 512 tasks due to 429s, immediate retry scheduled by orchestrator policy (backoff=0s)
[16:10:15] console: token_usage tenant=edgeforms spike delta=+120k tokens
(Attached: sanitized snippet of ingress logs and sample throttle headers provided by customer.)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: orchestrator configuration is aggressively retrying without jitter/backoff and the Private VPC edge is counting all replays against the same burst pool. Confirmed that healthchecks and preflight requests were NOT the dominant consumer. Observed that orchestrator was configured with zero jitter and maximum concurrency of 8 which aligns temporally with the spike. Edge rate-limiter counts per-route and tenant burst credits; background flushes were not isolated. We reproduced a smaller test in staging with identical orchestrator config and saw the same pattern. Potential mitigations: add jitter/exponential backoff in orchestrator, isolate webhook callbacks to a separate burst pool or priority lane, implement per-route smoothing for private deployments. Linked PRs propose adding jitter config and a priority tag to callbacks.

Asking for permanent configuration guidance and whether we can add dedicated burst-pool for callbacks on their private deployment.

resolution: Workaround implemented: temporary per-route smoothing on ingress and customer-side change to orchestrator to add exponential backoff with jitter. Result: immediate reduction of 429 waves. Permanent plan: (1) Product to evaluate support for configurable burst pools / priority lanes in Private deployments (tracked in linked PR and Confluence runbook), (2) Ops to add advice template to onboarding docs for customers using orchestrators: require jittered backoff and concurrency caps, (3) implement server-side per-route isolation for webhook paths as an opt-in setting for Private tier. Follow-up ticket to be opened to track product work and timeline.
